findings.reason: base.ts:170 now checks only addPath.oldPos - k < newLen. addPath sits on diagonal k+1 and newPos never drops below -1, so oldPos - k >= 0 always holds and behavior is the same as before. The invariant is also written down at base.ts:110-111 ('-1 <= newPos < newLen'), so the claim that nothing records it is wrong. This is a style point, not a defect in this change.
findings.claim: Dropping the 0 <= addPathNewPos guard leaves the add branch relying on an unstated invariant.
findings.evidence: The diff swaps the block `const addPathNewPos = addPath.oldPos - k; canAdd = addPath && 0 <= addPathNewPos && addPathNewPos < newLen;` for `const canAdd = addPath && addPath.oldPos - k < newLen;`. Reading the code around it, the change behaves the same today: addPath sits on diagonal k+1, so its newPos is addPath.oldPos - k - 1. The seed path starts at newPos -1, and addToPath and extractCommon never lower newPos, so addPath.oldPos - k is always >= 0. The only place this is written down is the general comment at lines 110-118 ('-1 <= oldPos < oldLen and -1 <= newPos < newLen'). The diff adds no test or assertion for the boundary, and `canAdd` is now typed as `Path | undefined | boolean` where it used to be a plain boolean.
